title: SRE stability huddle - sprint notes (2029-11-29)
content:
TL;DR:
- Two noteworthy incidents this week: a regional latency spike affecting hosted-api EU-west (partial 99p SLO breach) and a short-lived throttling cascade observed on a Dedicated pool after a config roll. No customer data exposure.
- Error budget burn: EU-west 99p latency consumed ~38% of weekly error budget; global token error budget steady.
- Runbook gap identified for model fallback orchestration (see Action items).
- Handoff: incoming oncall for week of 2029-12-03 assigned to Kai; outgoing notes and outstanding tasks below.

1) Incident summaries (concise)
- INC-2029-11-26-EU-LATENCY (SEV2 -> SEV3 resolved): 11/26 03:42–04:25 UTC. Symptoms: 99th percentile generation latency for small-context requests rose from baseline ~180ms to ~620ms for ~40 minutes in eu-west region. Root cause (post-mortem preliminary): a misweighted routing rule pushed a subset of low-latency traffic onto a legacy model variant with degraded kernel selection under the typical sequence profile. Mitigation: emergency reroute to verified model variant + temporary weight cap applied. Follow-up: validate routing weight calculation, add canary for routing changes.
- INC-2029-11-27-DEDICATED-THROTTLE (SEV3): 11/27 14:12–14:34 UTC. Symptoms: short burst of 429s from a dedicated capacity pool after a config push that mistakenly lowered the maximum inflight requests per worker. Mitigation: rollback of config and forced drain/rebalance. Impact: brief degradation for three enterprise customers on the pool; post-incident contact made by CS.

2) SLO / metrics snapshot (week ending 2029-11-29)
- Hosted API: 99p latency (global): target 600ms — observed 612ms (1.8% breach, driven by eu-west window).
- Hosted API: error rate (4xx/5xx) within SLA (0.12%).
- Dedicated pools: availability 99.95% (meets target) but one burst of throttles noted.
- Error budget: eu-west 99p remaining for the week: ~62%; projected risk if routing changes continue without canary.

Charts to check in console (links in linked_artifacts): 99p by region, inflight per-worker histogram, routing-weight heatmap.

3) On-call handoff (outgoing -> incoming)
- Outgoing (Maya): noted open items and escalation tips.
- Incoming (Kai): take ownership of the follow-ups below, monitor eu-west 99p closely first 48h, avoid ad-hoc routing weight changes during peak EU evening (18:00–22:00 CET).
- Outstanding tickets to watch: SRE-4123 (routing weight fix), SRE-4179 (dedicated pool config validation), SRE-4201 (add canary for model variant routing).
- Pager expectations: always page for >15min sustained 99p breach in production or any SEV2. SEV3 to be addressed within 30min and update bridge every 15min.

4) Action items (owners + ETA)
- SRE-4123: Fix routing weight calculation + add unit tests (Owner: Omar) - ETA: 2029-12-06.
- SRE-4201: Implement a lightweight canary (10% traffic) for routing rule changes (Owner: Lena) - ETA: 2029-12-04.
- Runbook update: Add explicit fallback criteria for model variant degradation and example curl commands for emergency reroute (Owner: Rohit) - ETA: 2029-12-02.
- Dedicated config gating: Add CI validation that rejects inflight limit drops >20% without approval (Owner: Platform Eng) - Proposal due 2029-12-09.
- Post-incident review: Draft and circulate detailed post-mortem for INC-2029-11-26 (Owner: Maya) - Draft ETA 2029-12-01.

5) Runbook / playbook notes
- Discovered runbook ambiguity: current fallback section assumes availability of variant A/B naming; our variant naming is sometimes generated dynamically and runbook examples fail to match. Temporary mitigation: added quick mapping script (scripts/runbook/variant-map) to the SRE repo — needs checkout and small doc.
- Added a small checklist for throttle events: 1) verify inflight limits, 2) check recent config PRs, 3) politely notify CS for impacted customers, 4) trigger emergency drain if config rollback required.

6) Communication & customer impact
- CS notified for the dedicated-pool incident; three customers saw increased 429s for <25 minutes. Support ticket templates updated to include observed time window and recommended mitigation text.
- No regulatory or security escalation necessary.

7) Observations and informal notes (huddle tone)
- We are seeing a recurring pattern where routing changes coincide with brief latency regressions. Hypothesis: routing logic lacks a short-term feedback loop that considers recent kernel performance signals.
- Quick experiment idea: feed last-10-min kernel success/failure metric into routing scoring for a short-lookback window. Could be a low-effort guardrail. (Not yet scoped.)
- Reminder: Avoid large routing weight reshuffles during global model refresh days — those coincide with slightly higher variance.

8) Quick wins / experiments for next week
- Add a small health probe that periodically runs a short generation workload to each model variant and emits a simple pass/fail metric for routing. (Owner: Omar, ETA 2029-12-03)
- CI gate for dedicated config changes (see Action items).

9) Handoff checklist (to be attached to rotation Slack thread)
- Confirm pager rules are unchanged.
- Share this doc and mark any updates in the Slack handoff thread.
- Run the local variant-map script once on the next oncall machine to ensure paths resolve.

Appendix A — links referenced:
- Post-mortem draft: https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/SRE/INC-2029-11-26-EU-LATENCY
- Jira: SRE-4123, SRE-4179, SRE-4201
- Repo: github.com/redwood/sre-runbooks (variant-map script at scripts/runbook/variant-map)

Appendix B — quick notes to self (rough):
- Need to coordinate with model-onboarding team to standardize variant stable names.
- Follow up with Console team to expose routing-weight deltas in the UI so non-SRE engineers can reason about changes before they roll.

End of notes.
